body:
The statistics propagator derives filters from inner/semi join bounds, but previously lost them when the binder cast a column to the common comparison type. For example, TPC-DS Q72 compares `CAST(inv_quantity_on_hand AS BIGINT) < cs_quantity`, so the known maximum of `cs_quantity` did not bound the inventory scan.

Derive these filters through invertible numeric casts using the existing cast capability checks. This includes integer and decimal widening, precision-safe conversions to floating point, and FLOAT to DOUBLE. Convert each bound back with the built-in cast; inclusive bounds remain conservative when conversion rounds, and the original join comparison remains in place. Unsupported conversions and TRY_CAST are skipped, and registered cast overrides retain their semantics. This stays within the numeric types supported by join-statistics tightening.

The author's original integral-cast benchmark reported Q72 at SF1000 improving from 56 s to 1.5 s, and at SF3000 inventory input dropping from 1.445B to about 139M rows. Those measurements predate the broader numeric coverage.

Validation: the join-statistics suite (55 cases), cast optimizer suite (9 cases), and three cast-pushdown tests pass with assertions and float-cast-overflow sanitization enabled. All 540 differential queries across 15 numeric type pairs match the previous PR head and optimizer-disabled execution, including rounding, precision boundaries, NaN, infinities, and NULLs. A 1M-row decimal-inequality microbenchmark improves from a 99 ms median to 21 ms with identical results; IMDB and TPC-DS were not rerun for this follow-up.
title: Derive join statistics filters through invertible numeric casts
